ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: Baozhi verse says not to cling to two sides or it

Senses.Explanation: The Middle Way is the course between or beyond opposed extremes. Yongming Yanshou’s compiled treatise says to proceed directly toward it; Baozhi’s verse says not to cling either to the two sides or to the Middle Way itself. Baizhang Huaihai makes the sharper Chan move: in a long inventory of learned attainments, even learning emptiness, equality, and the Middle Way can become an affliction when grasped as acquired understanding.

Senses.Note: In Huineng’s biography, Middle Way is adverbial: he asks how he could stop midway in seeking the great teaching. This is a journey-stage, not the named Middle Way.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: Huineng biography uses it for stopping midway

Senses.Explanation: Midway means partway along a course before its intended end. The compiler narrates Huineng’s resolve not to stop in mid-course and his departure the following day to seek instruction. The surrounding travel narrative supplies the governing frame: deciding not to halt is followed by setting out, meeting Zhiyuan, and proceeding onward.

Senses.Note: The phrase also appears in first-person retrospective description. One unnamed interlocutor says he was still "hazy and indistinct, bright and numinous, and had not yet obtained stability" (恍恍惚惚、昭昭靈靈，也未得個安穩); a later account says that this bright-and-numinous condition could not be made to arise and could not be found after a subsequent event. A verse asks, "what is the bright and numinous? By the time you blink, it has already been missed" (昭昭靈靈是什麼？眨得眼來已蹉過). Productive forms include "the bright-and-numinous one" (the nominal “bright-and-numinous one” form, 14 occurrences in 12 texts) and "recognize the bright and numinous" (認昭昭靈靈, 21 in 16). Eight texts preserve the sleep challenge's wording "the bright and numinous is your reality" (昭昭靈靈是汝真實).

Occurrences.Kwic: 豈容魔外家亂承當個昭昭靈靈識神為主人公
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B27/B27n0152.xml). Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄): Recorded Sayings of National Teacher Yulin (大覺普濟玉林禪師語錄), complete instruction under the record's own heading: Yulin Tongxiu warns against disorderly outsiders taking the bright-and-aware consciousness-spirit as the master within. The prior attribution to Juelang Daosheng was false.

Senses.Explanation: A reduplicated description: brightly evident (昭昭) and keenly numinous or responsive (靈靈), hence "bright and numinous." It is attested. Chinese Chan records frequently use the phrase while rejecting its identification with one's true self. One address asks, "if you recognize the bright and numinous as your reality, why does it no longer remain bright and numinous when you are asleep?" (汝若認昭昭靈靈是汝真實，為甚麼瞌睡時又不成昭昭靈靈). The same address gives a direct account: the bright and numinous arises because colors, sounds, scents, and other things before one are distinguished; without those things it is like "turtle fur and rabbit horns" (昭昭靈靈，祇因前塵色聲香等法而有分別；若無前塵，同於龜毛兔角). Another record states that the fault lies in taking the presently bright and numinous as correct, since it "arises dependent on encountered objects" (昭昭靈靈乃是緣境而有). These are the corpus's explicit predicates, not an entry-level theory of consciousness.

Senses.Explanation: Yuanwu denies that Huangbo’s public instruction is a contest over others wronging him or an act of self-display and self-praise. After Huangbo says that there is Chan but no teacher, Yuanwu Keqin asks where the statement lands. In explaining Xuedou’s verse, he says Huangbo’s instruction is not the headword and not self-assertion or self-praise; he then names moving freely in every direction, standing alone on a solitary peak, and appearing bodily in the busy market.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「是真語，是如語。」進云：「今日和尚登曲彔床，又舉揚何事？」師云：「不異語。」進云：「不須重說偈言。」便禮拜歸眾，師云：「孟八郎漢卻恁麼去也。」問：「一句了然超百億，如何今日又重宣？」師云：「為著阿誰？」進云：「恁麼則杖頭有眼分明在也。」師云：「做出便見。」問：「金牛飯、趙州茶，只為饑渴者，秪如不饑不渴底人來作麼生接待？」師打云：「也少你這一頓不得。」進云：「恁麼則一眾飽餐去也。」師云：「且道是何滋味？」僧便喝，師又打。問：「釋迦、彌勒猶是他奴，畢竟他是阿誰？」師云：「不識。」進云：「若然，則大千沙界任縱橫也。」師云：「且道他是阿誰？」僧喝，師打云：「鄭州出曹門。」問：「目前無法，意在目前。如何是目前法？」師打，云：「棒頭有眼。」進云：「因甚隱隱猶懷舊日嫌？」師云：「蒼天，蒼天。」進云：「莫把是非來入耳，從前知己反為讎。」師云：「自知較一半。」師乃云：「若論本分提綱，盡十方界無有針鋒許不是當人真實之體，有甚根塵器界、罪行福行而不一切智智清淨？古人道箇『眾罪如霜露，慧日能消除。』已屬剩語，此外更有所說，何異捏目生花？事不獲已，與汝箇真實指注。」驀豎拂子，云：「看，看！只這箇，名不得、狀不得、聖凡他不得、是非他不得，除是絕羅籠、出窠臼底衲僧向威音那畔一逴逴得，便轉向今世門頭大行闊步，便恁麼去，魔宮佛國任性逍遙，地獄天堂隨緣放曠，自然綽綽然有餘裕。

Senses.Explanation: Putting another head atop one's head means adding a needless construction to what is already present. Huishan Jiexian applies it to turning expedient training procedures into a fixed method, pairing it with speaking of a dream inside a dream. Yikui Yuankui uses it when the forms before the assembly are additionally called Buddha. Yinyuan Longqi makes the naming problem explicit: calling the raised staff a staff adds a head, but refusing the name seeks life apart from the head. Shengke Deyu gives the phrase as his answer to 'what is Buddha?' and sets it against 'cut off the head to seek life.' A lamp recension of Linji Yixuan supplies the pointed question behind the image: after seekers add what is unnecessary, what do they lack?

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan (無準師範禪師語錄), in the section headed 'Fojian Chan Master's recorded sayings from his first residence at Qingliang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture' (佛鑑禪師初住慶元府清凉禪寺語錄): Wuzhun Shifan addresses the stewards, senior monastic officers, elders, and assembly and wishes each of them well. Here Fojian is Wuzhun Shifan's title; the record later self-identifies him as (師範) and names him (佛鑑範公).

Senses.Explanation: The head officers are the monastery's senior west-rank officers. One regulation names the category's offices—chief seat, secretary, librarian, guest prefect, and bath prefect—and prescribes how they are invited and escorted into their quarters. Other rules make them lead the assembly and forbid the assembly from taking position before them; public addresses distinguish them from the stewards while calling both groups to act.
